title: Taiwanese American Students Association at Johns Hopkins University
content_html:
The Taiwanese American Students Association at Johns Hopkins University (jhuTASA) is a student organization at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, Maryland. Its founding year is not documented in available first-party sources, though the organization’s official mascot, Tubs — a Taiwanese black bear — was created in 2019. jhuTASA primarily serves Taiwanese American students while welcoming all who wish to connect with Taiwanese culture and community.

According to its Hopkins Groups directory page, jhuTASA is committed to bringing a bit of Taiwan to campus and the greater Baltimore community. The organization operates a family system designed to foster close-knit community bonds among members. Its signature annual events include Tour of Taiwan and Night Market — featuring homemade Taiwanese dishes, games, performances, and prizes — as well as recurring programming such as arts and crafts sessions, dessert nights, bread fundraisers, and an annual trip to Rockville, Maryland.

jhuTASA also participates in the broader Taiwanese American student network through the Intercollegiate Taiwanese American Students Association (ITASA). The organization hosted the ITASA East Coast Conference (ITASA ECC 2021) in February 2021, under the theme “Sketching Your Own Path,” and has sent representatives to multiple prior ECCs. jhuTASA is formally recognized by the Johns Hopkins Office of Multicultural Affairs and is listed among the university’s multicultural student organizations. The organization maintains an active Instagram account (@jhutasa) and a Facebook page.
